title: Beyond the 956: Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys bass voice behind ‘Elvira,’ dies at 83
excerpt: Richard Sterban, the deep bass voice of the Oak Ridge Boys whose “oom papa mow mow” made “Elvira” a country classic, died November 14, 2026, at 83 in Hendersonville, Tennessee, after a long battle with cancer. His family and the Oak Ridge Boys announced his death.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Richard Sterban, the deep bass voice of the Oak Ridge Boys whose rumbling “oom papa mow mow” turned “Elvira” into one of the most recognizable songs in country music, has died at 83.

Sterban died Saturday, November 14, 2026, in Hendersonville, Tennessee, from complications of bronchitis and pneumonia after a long battle with cancer, according to his family and the Oak Ridge Boys, who announced his death. He had been treated for pancreatic cancer, which he revealed in September 2025.

Born Richard Anthony Sterban on April 24, 1943, in Camden, New Jersey, he grew up in nearby Collingswood singing gospel music. He joined the Oak Ridge Boys in late 1972, leaving a job singing with J. D. Sumner and the Stamps Quartet behind Elvis Presley to chase a goal he had set for himself as a young man.

For more than five decades, Sterban anchored one of America’s most beloved vocal groups. His bass solo on the group’s 1981 hit “Elvira” became one of the most familiar sounds in American music, and his lead vocal on the group’s cover of “Dream On” reached the top ten. In 2015, Sterban and his bandmates were inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame.

He stepped back from touring in May 2025 as he received cancer treatment, but returned to the stage with the group at the Grand Ole Opry on January 30 and 31, 2026, to sing “Elvira” to a standing ovation. He also sang on several tracks of the group’s October 2026 album, Buried Treasures.

“We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers. Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time; we find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus,” his family said in a statement. Funeral arrangements will be announced later.

Sources: The Oak Ridge Boys and the Sterban family; The Music Universe; Whiskey Riff; Country Rebel; Hendersonville Standard; Deadline.
